note:
Two 1901 households from one enumerator's page, transcribed from the image A. Hagues sent. Neither schedule gives a house, so both are added unfiled under the address the return gives, with the directory evidence in the address so they can be filed with a click.

Schedule 135, North Road: Adelheid Weinberg, widow, born in Schleswig-Holstein and naturalised British, with her sons Mehir and Harry, lace manufacturers and shipping merchants, and two servants. Mehir (#702) and Harry Judah (#2830) are already in the record and are bound by number. The house is almost certainly 4 North Road (#412): the next schedule on the page, 136, is headed '5 North Road'; Wright's Directory prints 'Mrs. Adelaide' and Harry J. Weinberg at 4 North Road in 1913-14 and 1915-16; and Harry's probate calls him 'late of 4 North Road'. In 1894-95 and 1898-99 the directory has Jacob Weinberg, of Simon, May & Co., on North Road without a number, likely her late husband. Mehir had moved to Hardwicke House by 1911.

Schedule 137, Cavendish Crescent North: Walter S. Hunt, lace manufacturer, with his wife Susanne, her sister Emily Mottershal (the return says sister-in-law to the head, and both were born in Lincoln), Emily C. and Herbert Mottershal, niece and nephew, and two servants. Walter (#3203) is already in the record and is bound by number. The house is very likely Castlemount, 20 Cavendish Crescent North (#35): Wright's Directory 1898-99 prints 'Castle mount, Walter S. Hunt, of Hunt, Moody & Co.', and Castlemount holds no 1901 census record. In 1894-95 he was at 15 Cavendish Crescent South.

Readings to check against the image: Mottershal (it may be Mottershead) and the servant Constance Herrick, whose surname runs off the bottom of the page. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1901 census, North Road and Cavendish Crescent North, schedules 135 and 137, from the enumerator's page sent by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, pages 44 and 103 (Leicester Special Collections ids 164550, 164609); 1898-99, pages 50 and 111 (ids 165226, 165287); 1913-14, page 165 (id 166521); 1915-16, page 168 (id 347809).
